cohort: Pregnant women from the 2007-2018 National Inpatient Sample, with and without Listeria infection
finding: Pregnant women with Listeria infection had a 21.2-fold higher risk of severe maternal morbidity, including sepsis, septic shock, and acute respiratory distress syndrome, as well as higher rates of preterm birth and stillbirth.
mod_finding: Women with Listeria infection were also more likely to have a cesarean delivery.
